subject of two incompatible okimtot (25b.11, 25b.14); commits nothing directly

props.gloss_en: R' Yehuda: the Akavya-Sages dispute over shed hair is where the animal was then slaughtered
R' Yosei: not there; the dispute is where the animal then died
wool dangling on a firstborn: what appears with the shearing is permitted
and what does not appear with the shearing is forbidden
(entertained) by implication of R' Yosei's 'not in this', Akavya forbids [the wool] where the animal was slaughtered
where he slaughtered it, all agree [the wool] is permitted; they dispute where it died
the dispute is where an expert permitted [the animal]
one master holds: we decree, lest he come to delay it
and one master holds: we do not decree
but where no expert permitted it, all agree it is forbidden
blemished ones [mixed in] forbid in any amount
and R' Yosei says: let it be examined
(entertained) 'let it be examined' means: [find] the blemished one and remove it
here we deal with the shearings of a blemished firstborn mixed with ordinary shearings
the first tanna is R' Yehuda, who says: [where] they were slaughtered, the Rabbis forbid
and R' Yosei follows his own view, who says: [where] they were slaughtered, the Rabbis permit
Rav Sheshet: 'let it be examined' -- is it not whether it is a permanent or a passing blemish, even though no expert permitted it?
Rava: no -- 'let it be examined' whether an expert permitted it: if so, yes; if not, no
R' Chiyya bar Abba's R' Yochanan: the dispute is where he examined and did not find
and they dispute as R' Meir and the Rabbis dispute
R' Meir: whatever was presumed impure remains in its impurity until the impurity becomes known
and the Sages say: he digs until he reaches rock or virgin soil
R' Asi's R' Yochanan: the dispute is where he examined and found
and they dispute as Rebbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel dispute
a field in which a grave was lost: one who enters it is impure
Rebbi: if a grave was found in it, one who enters is pure -- I say the grave that was lost is the grave that was found
RSBG: the whole field must be examined
R' Asi's ground: impurity may have been carried off by a raven or a mouse; but a blemished animal -- where would it go?
the other's counter: say it was a passing blemish, and it healed
R' Chiyya bar Abba's ground: a field is a usual burial place, so another may have been buried; but consecrated animals, once examined and whole -- is it their way to develop a blemish?
the other's counter: since they butt each other, a blemish is common among them
one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn, even though it then developed a blemish and he slaughtered it -- forbidden
a blemished firstborn from which he plucked [wool] and then it died -- Akavya permits and the Sages forbid
but specifically the Sages said: let him set it in the window, perhaps there is hope
(entertained) R' Yosei's view is the same as the first tanna's
(entertained) the first tanna and R' Yosei differ over an expert's permission: the first tanna requires it, R' Yosei does not
Rava: no -- all agree: if an expert permitted it, yes; if not, no
Rava: the first tanna holds they dispute the dead one and the same for the slaughtered one; that they are shown disputing the dead one is to show you Akavya's strength
R' Yehuda holds: where it died, all agree it is forbidden
Rav Nachman: the halakha is as R' Yehuda
the בחירתא mishna: hair of a blemished firstborn that shed, set in a window, and then he slaughtered it -- Akavya permits, the Sages forbid
(entertained) the dangling-wool clause is R' Yosei's
rather, plainly the clause is R' Yehuda's
(entertained) [on R' Yehuda] the clause speaks of an animal that died
rather, it speaks of an animal he slaughtered
(entertained) the clause is Akavya's [in the slaughtered case]
rather, it is the Rabbis'
a sin or guilt offering is no question: since they come for atonement, one does not delay them
a firstborn or tithe is no question either: since they do not come for atonement, one delays them
(candidate answer) wool torn out of an unblemished burnt offering is permitted

questions.gloss_en: R' Yannai: wool torn out of an unblemished burnt offering -- what is its law? (the stam first reformulates: תולש? מי איכא מאן דשרי -- rather, נתלש). Since atonement is not its main purpose, one delays it; or, since it too atones for a positive commandment, one does not? The תא שמע at 26b.2 is deflected and no answer follows

supports.gloss_en: הואיל ותנן בבחירתא כוותיה -- the preferred mishna puts the dispute in the slaughtered case, as R' Yehuda does (tanya_kevatei is the nearest kind for a תנן כוותיה)

מתניתין נמי דייקא: the dangling-wool clause (permitted if it appears with the shearing, forbidden if not) fits only the Rabbis in the slaughtered case -- so the dispute is in the slaughtered case, as R' Yehuda has it (26a.10-13; elimination steps are hypotheses h_med_*)
תא שמע: התולש צמר מבכור תם ... אסור -- טעמא דתולש, הא נתלש שרי, וכל שכן עולה דלא משהי לה (the a fortiori rides here; header)

deflected_by.gloss_en: הוא הדין אפילו נתלש נמי אסור; והאי דקתני תולש -- להודיעך כחו דעקביא, דבבעל מום אפילו בתולש נמי שרי. Itself challenged and defended (26b.4, schema gap -- header): והאנן נשר תנן! -- תנא נשר להודיעך כחן דרבנן, תנא תולש להודיעך כחו דעקביא

objections.gloss_en: מתיב רב ששת: ... ורבי יוסי אומר יבקר -- with the baraita construed of a blemished firstborn's shearings (25b.8), יבוקר means whether the blemish is permanent or passing, אף על גב שלא התירו מומחה (25b.9): R' Yosei permits without an expert

answered_by.gloss_en: לא; יבוקר -- אי התירו מומחה אין, ואי לא לא (= p_rava_yevukar_hitiro)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: התולש צמר מבכור תם ... אסור; טעמא דתם, הא בעל מום שרי, אף על פי שלא התירו מומחה!

answered_by.gloss_en: תנא: כל היכא דלא התירו מומחה -- תם קרי ליה: the tanna calls 'unblemished' whatever no expert permitted
